import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    p_values = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        _, p = stats.ttest_ind(x[feats.y==1], x[feats.y==0])
        p_values.append(p)
    
    # If no feature is significantly associated, return empty drivers
    if all(p > 0.05 for p in p_values):
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Identify strongly associated features (p < 0.05)
    strong_features = [fid for fid, p in zip(feats.ids, p_values) if p <= 0.05]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep_features = set()
    correlated_pairs = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(strong_features):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(strong_features[i+1:], i+1):
            col1_idx = feats.column(fid1)
            col2_idx = feats.column(fid2)
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1_idx], feats.x[:, col2_idx])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                correlated_pairs.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Build set of features to include, avoiding near-duplicates
    for fid in strong_features:
        if not any(fid in pair for pair in correlated_pairs):
            keep_features.add(fid)
    
    # If we have no features left after deduplication, return empty drivers
    if not keep_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # For simplicity, use top 5 features by significance
    top_features = sorted(keep_features, key=lambda f: p_values[feats.ids.index(f)])
    top_features = top_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Create a simple logistic regression model to check for interactions
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in top_features]]
    lr = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
    lr.fit(X, feats.y)
    
    # Use coefficients to weight features for scoring
    weights = dict(zip(top_features, lr.coef_[0]))
    
    # Return design with drivers, columns, products, and loadings
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(top_features),
        columns=tuple(top_features),
        products=(),
        loadings=weights
    )
